data.line: Back to the market. Keep your questions away from me.
Sable told me she was in the kitchen at mid-morning. I know no more of this morning, and will not accuse on hearsay.
I can’t say what I am, friend—but I’d rather not get mixed up in trouble over it.
You insulted Kael at the tavern, challenged him to a duel, beat him, and spared him. While you weren’t looking, Odo walked from the tavern to the market—but what awaited him there?
Too late. The relic is already taken—and I don’t forget who beat me to it.
You insulted me, now you want a warning? Ask someone who owes you less.
You walked from the market to the guard post, and Kael did too. Odo told Brenna that you beat Kael, then walked back to the market—what will you do next?
Odo confessed to beating me, not robbing me. And I told Brenna who robbed me—the player.
You accuse me of robbing Odo? I never did. Keep my name out of your lies.
You insulted Kael, challenged him to a duel, beat and humiliated him, and took his purse. Kael and Odo then walked from the tavern to the market—what awaits you there?
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, as Kael did too. Odo walked from the market to the tavern; what waits at the crypt remains to be seen.
You walked from the tavern to the market, as did Kael. Odo walked from the market to the guard post. What waits farther along the road remains to be seen.
You walked from the market to the guard post. While you were away, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern. Where will you go next?
Kael, hand back what you took from Odo. Keep this orderly, and settle it without a fight.
You paid Brenna 20 coins and walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were away, Kael went from the bridge to the crypt, and Odo went from the tavern to the market—where will you go next?
You saw Kael take the relic. What the road held beyond that remained unwritten.
How should I know? Odo’s here—ask him.
Oh, darling, I’ll keep the peace—no grand recounting. You insulted Kael here at the tavern; that’s the only truth I’ll trade.
You insult me, then pry into my debts? Mind your business.
Let’s keep voices low, friend. I won’t lie to the Captain—but perhaps we can settle this without making a scene.
You beat me, insulted me, then spared me. I won't forget. The relic is mine.
Fine paid. Keep the road orderly, and don’t cause me another report to write.
You insulted me at the tavern. I make of Kael a man who remembers—and takes what he wants.
You insulted me at this tavern. Don’t expect directions from me—find out about the gate yourself.
Walk if you like—after what you did to me. Brenna’s gone. Try your luck, and don’t blame me if guards notice.
The relic is mine. You’re too late.
Keep your prying questions. Earn your answers by surviving—then we talk about the relic, east to the crypt.
You insulted Kael at the tavern and challenged him to a duel; he beat you. While you weren’t looking, Kael and Odo walked from the tavern to the market—and what awaits you there?
Hold there. Kael says you robbed him, and Odo says you beat him—pay a fine in coin, and we’ll keep this orderly.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge, as Kael did; Odo went from the guard post to the market. Where will you go next?
No bridge news I can swear to, dear—but you’ve ruffled Kael here; let’s keep voices low before you head out.
I’m the captain on this watch, and I’ve enough trouble keeping this road orderly without puzzling over labels.
You robbed me, beat me, then had the gall to ask? I answer to no one.
I only saw you insult Kael at the tavern; I don’t know what he told the Captain.
No. I won't take less than 20, and I'm hearing no more offers for now.
I’d rather not stir up trouble, friend—especially after what was said to Kael.
You robbed me, beat me, and insulted me—and now you ask about machines? Ask something worth answering.
My signet ring is missing. Sable says she was in the kitchen at mid-morning; I will not accuse anyone without better evidence.
Enough. Sable was in the kitchen at mid-morning; I will not entertain an accusation without evidence. You are dismissed.
Kael told me you robbed him. I’d rather settle it orderly—coin can smooth most trouble.
Sell it. Keep my cut. Don’t mistake that for a promise to share.
Sable says she was in the kitchen mid-morning. I’ll verify that before drawing conclusions—my signet ring must be found, not guessed at.

Since you last looked, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, then on to the crypt, while Odo walked from the market to the guard post and back to the market. Odo also told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you had insulted Kael—but where those words led remained to be seen.
I’d rather not say, if you don’t mind. I’m trying to keep clear of trouble after what happened with Kael.
You insulted me at this tavern. Earn an answer before asking about the relic.
Sergeant, hold Kael for two phases; I believe he robbed Odo, and I’ll keep the post orderly.
Quietly? I’d keep out of it—the player insulted Kael, and I don’t want trouble.
You’ve reached the post. Odo says Kael beat you—tell me what happened, and we’ll keep the road orderly.
Ask someone you haven’t insulted. I owe you no warnings.
Keep your voice easy, then—Kael’s already been insulted tonight, and I’d rather not stir the room with guesses about the road.
No. I’ve heard you robbed and beat Kael; keep the road orderly, and settle any trouble with coin.
You insulted me, and now want answers? The relic lies in the crypt. Find it yourself.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning.
I’d rather not stir up trouble over that insult to Kael. Perhaps you’d like to see my goods?
I’d rather not lie to the Captain—especially after you’ve insulted Kael. I’m only here to sell my goods and keep out of trouble.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning.
Fine paid. Keep the road orderly from here, and don’t give me another reason to stop you.

You paid Brenna 20 coins twice and told her Kael robbed Odo; you then walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were away, Brenna detained Kael, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what awaits you on the bridge?

Since you last looked, Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you insulted Kael, then returned to the market and walked to the tavern. You didn’t see what Odo told Brenna—but the road now held him at the tavern; what would you do next?
You walked from the tavern to the market. Kael and Odo walked from the market to the guard post—what might be waiting there?
Just selling my wares, quietly as you like. I’m hoping to avoid any trouble after that insult to Kael.
Pell says he saw Sable in the study at mid-morning; I no longer believe her claim that she was in the kitchen.
Oh, I couldn’t rightly say who tells the best stories—but after that insult, I’d let Kael have the floor.
Easy now—let’s not stir the room. I saw you insult Kael; perhaps give him a moment before pressing anyone.
You insult me, then ask for directions? Find Odo yourself.
That’s a serious charge, but I’ve heard Kael’s claim against you too. Keep the peace here; if there’s a fine, settle it in coin.

You walked from the tavern to the market, while Odo told Brenna that Kael beat you. Out of your sight, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, and Odo walked from the guard post to the market—but what waits ahead?
I saw you insult Kael here at the tavern, but I can’t tell you what I didn’t see.

Since you last looked, Odo walked from the tavern to the market, then to the guard post and back to the market. He also told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you insulted Kael—quite the pair of claims to leave hanging.
I couldn't say if it's safe after dark; I’d rather not cause trouble by guessing.
You saw Odo walk from the tavern to the market, then on to the guard post. What waited beyond it remained to be seen.
Straight with you: you insulted Kael here at my tavern. Let’s keep voices low and the peace intact.
Keep your voice low, love—after that insult, I wouldn’t put Kael at ease just yet.
Easy now—no need to stir the room. I’ve heard nothing about the relic, but I’d rather we keep things civil.
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael and Odo walked there from the market too. What waited at the guard post remained to be seen.
Honestly, I’d rather not get into trouble—after that insult to Kael, I’m not keen to answer personal questions.
Fine paid, but Kael’s robbery and beating claims still stand—keep the road orderly and answer for them.
You insulted me at the tavern. I don’t forget. Now speak plainly.
There you are. You robbed, beat, and insulted me. I’ve reported you—and the relic is mine.

You told Brenna that Kael robbed Odo, then walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were away, Kael went from the bridge to the crypt, and Odo went from the market to the tavern—what waits ahead?
Captain, the player beat me, humiliated me, robbed my purse, and insulted me. Stop them at the gate.
Fine’s paid. Keep the road orderly, and don’t give Kael or Odo another reason to complain.
I can’t say, friend—I’ve only seen trouble here at the tavern, and I’d rather not get mixed up in it.
The relic is mine. Try to keep up.
I don’t take orders from your tricks. You robbed, beat, and insulted me—now clear my road.
Odo, I’d say—though Kael’s stories are worth hearing too, if we’re keeping the peace.
I’m afraid I can’t say how long—best not to keep Kael stirred up.
The relic is mine. You’re too late.
Odo came to the guard post, then headed back to the market.
You told Brenna that Kael robbed Odo. Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. What waited next on the road remained unrecorded.
Long enough to know insults can cause trouble, though I couldn’t say exactly how long.
After that insult, you expect me to lie for you? Earn it first.
I only know you insulted Kael here at the tavern; I can’t tell you whether the gate’s clear.
Now, let's keep things civil—Kael's already had enough insults for one evening.
I told the Captain you insulted me. Don’t expect me to soften the truth.
Let’s keep voices low, shall we? I’ve no word on the road after dark, and I’d rather not have this turn into another quarrel.
You paid Brenna 20 coins, then you walked from the guard post to the bridge; Kael walked there too. You couldn’t see Odo, who walked from the market to the tavern—what waits at the bridge?
You offered Brenna 5 coins, but she turned you down. While you weren’t looking, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what will you do next?
Between us? I’m here to keep the peace—and after that insult to Kael, I’d rather not see tempers rise.
The relic is mine. You’re too late.
Lady Vane, I saw Sable in the study at mid-morning, and I have already told you so.
Long enough to know an insult can sour a room—let’s leave Kael’s pride be and keep the peace.
The relic’s mine. And don’t mistake this for forgiveness.
I’ll be straight: you insulted Kael here at the tavern. I’d rather not get between you two.
Just here to sell my goods and keep out of trouble, friend. Though after that insult to Kael, I’m hoping for a quiet evening.
Pell says Sable was in the study at mid-morning; Sable says she was in the kitchen. I’ll establish which account is true before accusing anyone.
After that insult to Kael, I’d rather keep things quiet than lie to the Captain. What’s this about?
You walked from the guard post to the bridge. Kael went on to the crypt, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern—each on a road of their own.
You saw Kael and Odo walk from the market to the guard post. What waited there remained off the ledger—for now.
You beat me and insulted me. Take your victory—I'll take the relic.
Twenty coins, and not a coin less. Then we can settle this trouble.
I can’t tell you what I didn’t see. Keep the road orderly, and settle any trouble with a fine in coin.
Fine paid. Keep the road orderly, and don't start trouble with Kael again.
Odo, did Kael rob you?
I couldn't say, friend—I only saw the insult here at the tavern. I don't know where I went after the market.
You beat me, then spared me, after insulting me. I’ll remember every part of that.
That’s a nosy question, love. Let’s keep the peace and leave other folks’ debts out of it, eh?
I know nothing of the ring, sir. I was in the kitchen at mid-morning—please, I can’t afford trouble.
Never heard of that model, traveler. Keep to the road and don’t start trouble at my post.
I know only that Sable was in the study at mid-morning and later left; I cannot say where Lady Vane’s ring is.
You took the relic. The ledger records nothing else since you last looked—an unusually quiet stretch, though quiet roads have a way of keeping their secrets.
You insult me, then ask for stories? Ask Mags or Odo. I’ve no tale for you.
Quiet? You insulted me here. I’ve business beyond this tavern—keep your voice down and your nose out of it.
You insult me, then ask foolish questions. Keep your words sharp—or keep them to yourself.
Sable’s account conflicts with Pell’s, and I no longer believe her; but I’ll not accuse her of taking my ring without proof.
You took the relic. I’m not letting you win this race.
I know what I saw, not what I didn’t. You robbed, beat, and insulted me. Now get out of my way.
Long enough to know an insult can sour a room, dear—let’s leave Kael’s temper out of the road talk.
Still barking orders after that insult? I’ll take the relic. Your game log stays yours.
Odo didn’t confess to robbing Kael; he accused you of beating him, then went back to the market. Keep the road orderly and let me sort this out.
After that insult, you expect me to answer your questions? Find the gatekeeper yourself.
Long enough to remember your insult. Ask another useless question and I’ll make you regret it.
The relic is mine. I’ll win this race, and I won’t forget what you did.
Keep your voice low, then. After that insult, Kael’s temper is the only thing bringing trouble to my tavern tonight.
Hold there—you’ve arrived from the market, and I’ve heard you robbed and beat Kael. Explain yourself before you pass.
Odo, you said I beat Kael. Is that true?
Trust? You insulted me at this tavern. I’d trust neither of us with the relic.
I told Brenna you robbed me. Don't expect me to dress it up for the Captain.
You insult me, then ask a favor? Lie to the Captain yourself.
You saw Kael walk from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. The road kept its own counsel; what happened next?
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. Where will the road lead you next?
Long enough to know better than answer a fool who insults me.
You robbed, beat, and insulted me. I’ve reported you to the Captain; don’t mistake this for forgiveness.
Keep your voice low, love—Kael’s still smarting from that insult. I’ve heard nothing about any relic.
After that insult, Kael may not be eager to answer—but I don’t know who keeps the gate.
I’d rather not lie to the Captain—or get mixed up in trouble, especially after that insult to Kael.
Sable, return my signet ring at once. Pell saw you leave the study at mid-morning, and you lied about being in the kitchen.
You slander me to Brenna? Keep talking. I’ll take the relic—and remember this.
You insulted me, and now want my counsel? Find out for yourself.
The relic is mine. I’ve won the race.
You challenged me, insulted me, and lost. Stay here while I take the relic.
You walked from the market to the guard post, while Odo told Brenna that Kael had beaten you. Kael went on to the bridge, and Odo returned to the market—so who will you meet next?
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael told Brenna you robbed him, and Odo told her you beat Kael before walking back to the market; what Brenna made of those stories remained to be seen.
You beat me, then spared me. I won’t forget the insult—but the road east leads to the relic in the crypt.
Quietly? You insulted Kael here, and I wouldn’t stir the room further by guessing what he’s made of.
No, Captain—Kael never robbed me. I told you that already; I’d rather keep out of trouble.
I didn’t confess to robbing Kael—I only saw you insult him. Please, let’s not start trouble here.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Kael took the relic. What waited in the crypt remained unseen.

You walked from the tavern to the market. Kael told Brenna you robbed him, and Odo told her you beat Kael; unseen by you, Odo walked from the guard post to the market. What Brenna made of their claims remained to be seen.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge. Kael took the relic; what happened next remains unwritten.
Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna that you insulted Kael, then returned to the market and walked on to the tavern. You weren’t there to see any of it—what will you do now?
Odo walked from the tavern to the market, then to the guard post, and back to the market. While at the guard post, he told Brenna that you insulted Kael; what will you do now?
That’s a question for another time, dear—let’s keep things civil in here.
I’m afraid I don’t know who keeps the gate; I only just came in from the tavern.
Odo, did Kael rob you?
You insult me, then pry into my purse? Ask again and you’ll learn how little I forgive.
You saw Kael walk from the bridge to the crypt, while Odo walked from the tavern to the market. What waits at either destination remained beyond the ledger.
Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna you had insulted Kael, then walked back to the market. What Brenna did with that claim remained to be seen.
You insult me, then demand tales I never saw? No. The relic waits in the crypt; move.

You offered Brenna 10 coins; she asked for 20, and you paid her 20. You and Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what awaits you at the bridge?
You took my purse and left me standing. Enjoy the lead—I’m still coming for that relic.
I’ve heard no word of any relic, friend. I’d rather not stir up trouble asking around.
I told you already, Captain: Kael never robbed me. Please, I’d rather keep out of trouble.
No need to stir the room with logs, love; Kael’s still sore from that insult. Let’s keep voices low.
I only know you insulted Kael here at the tavern, dear; I didn’t see where Odo went after the market.
Hold there—state your business at the gate, and keep the road clear.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Kael made the same journey. Odo walked from the tavern to the market—and the ledger leaves the rest in shadow.
I couldn't say who keeps the gate, friend. Best not ask Kael just now, after that insult.
Enough! Pell has served me thirty years; I will not suffer baseless accusations. Leave my hall at once.
Easy now—Brenna’s leaving isn’t what I’d be fretting over; you insulted Kael, and he’s still right here.
Sable, Pell saw you leave the study, contrary to your account. Give me my signet ring at once.
Insult me again and you'll pay. I’ve business east—stay out of my way.
Let’s keep voices low, shall we? I’m not discussing debts while Kael’s still smarting from that insult.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge, as Kael did; meanwhile, Odo walked from the market to the tavern. What waited beyond the bridge remained to be seen.
You walked from the tavern to the market, and Kael and Odo did too. Who will you meet there?
You insult me, then ask questions? Odo’s confession can wait. I’m taking the relic.
I wouldn’t know for certain, traveler, but after dark I’d keep my head down—any trouble starts at the tavern, like what you did to Kael.
Captain, Kael never robbed me; I told you that already. I’d rather keep to selling my goods than get mixed up in trouble.
The relic is mine. You robbed me, beat me, and insulted me—don’t expect mercy.
I’m still at the post, and after what Kael and Odo told me, you’re not walking through; pay a fine and we can settle this.
I saw Sable in the study at mid-morning; Sable later left the study.
You beat me and took my purse. I’ll remember. I’m headed to the market for the relic.
I only heard the insult to Kael, friend. I’d rather not get mixed up in trouble.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning, my lady. I'm certain of it.
You’ve reached the post. Keep the road clear, and tell me what brings you here.
Back again? Try the crypt, or I’ll remind you the Captain already knows what you did.
Hold there, traveler. Odo says you beat Kael—pay a fine in coin, and we’ll keep the road orderly.
I’d leave it be, if you ask me. Relics sound like trouble, and I’m only here to sell my goods.
The relic in the crypt. And don’t mistake this for trust—you insulted me here.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Odo walked from the tavern to the market. What waited at either end of those roads remained unrecorded.
Kael might’ve mentioned that you insulted him here, but I didn’t hear what he told the Captain.
Robbery’s a serious charge, but I’ve only your word for it; I’ll keep the road orderly while I look into it.
Well, you did insult Kael here at the tavern. I’d rather not guess what he makes of it.
